RESIDUAL DISCHARGE.

At any instant we have
$$E=a_{1} r_{1} p_{1}+a_{2} r_{2} p_{2}+\text { \&c. }+R_{0} u=0$$
(26)
and also, by (3),
$$u=p_{1}+\frac{d f_{1}}{d t} .$$
(27)
Hence $\quad\left(R+R_{0}\right) u=a_{1} r_{1} \frac{d f_{1}}{d t}+a_{2} r_{2} \frac{d f_{2}}{d t}+$ \&c.
(28)
Integrating with respect to $t$ in order to find $Q$, we get
$$\left(R+R_{0}\right) Q=a_{1} r_{1}\left(f_{1}^{\prime}-f_{1}\right)+a_{2} r_{2}\left(f_{2}^{\prime}-f_{2}\right)+\& \mathrm{c} .,$$
(29)
where $f_{1}$ is the initial, and $f_{1}^{\prime}$ the final value of $f_{1}$.
In this case $f_{1}^{\prime}=0$, and by (2) and (20) $f_{1}=E_{0}\left(\frac{r_{1}}{4 \pi k_{1} R}-C\right)$.
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}
\left(R+R_{0}\right) Q & =-\frac{E}{4 \pi R}\left(\frac{a_{1} r_{1}^{2}}{k_{1}}+\frac{a_{2} r_{2}^{2}}{k_{2}}+\text { \&c. }\right)+E_{0} C R, \\
& =-\frac{C E_{0}}{R} \Sigma \Sigma\left[a_{1} a_{2} k_{1} k_{2}\left(\frac{r_{1}}{k_{1}}-\frac{r_{2}}{k_{2}}\right)\right],
\end{aligned}$$
(30)
(31)
where the summation is extended to all quantities of this form
belonging to every pair of strata.
It appears from this that $Q$ is always negative, that is to say,
in the opposite direction to that of the current employed in
charging the system.
This investigation shews that a dielectric composed of strata
of different kinds may exhibit the phenomena known as electric
absorption and residual discharge, although none of the sub-
stances of which it is made exhibit these phenomena when
alone. An investigation of the cases in which the materials are
arranged otherwise than in strata would lead to similar results,
though the calculations would be more complicated, so that we
may conclude that the phenomena of electric absorption may be
expected in the case of substances composed of parts of different
kinds, even though these individual parts should be micro-
scopically small *.
It by no means follows that every substance which exhibits
this phenomenon is so composed, for it may indicate a new kind
of electric polarization of which a homogeneous substance may

* \{Rowland and Nichols have shewn that crystals of Iceland Spar whick are very
homogeneous shew no Electric Absorption, Phil. Mug. xi. p. 414, 1881. Muraoka
found that while paraffin and xylol shewed no residual charge when separate, a layer
of xylol on a layer of paraffin did. Wied. Ann. 40, 381, 1890.\}
